subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` permanently fail closed on legacy ownerless rows, accepting that those rows require a non-plugin operator recovery path?
rationale: The code cannot safely infer which plugin owns an ownerless persisted row; allowing adoption weakens isolation, while rejection intentionally breaks previously possible plugin-runtime mutations.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Keep exact-owner equality, document that operators or non-plugin clients must repair or replace ownerless rows, and require deployed proof before merge.

options.title: Add explicit recovery flow
options.body: Delay merge until a narrow operator-authorized adoption or migration mechanism is designed and tested without permitting arbitrary plugin takeover.

options.title: Coordinate ownership work
options.body: Pause this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103148 until one shared ownership helper and ownerless-row policy cover all session mutation paths.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Keep exact-owner equality, document that operators or non-plugin clients must repair or replace ownerless rows, and require deployed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available current-history signal for the sessions.patch surface, though final security-policy authority is not established by the available evidence.
